spec.section:
## Preconditions
The local owner decides whether the peer is trusted and whether requests are automatic, proposal-only, or approval-gated. Connectivity is not authority. Obtain the peer's stable id, owner, mTLS public key or signed-token reference, expiry, allowed scopes, dedupe namespace, and local approval route.

## Procedure
1. Authenticate and validate the credential; reject expired or malformed identity. 2. Write a `FederationMap` through the controller with revision, scopes, actor mapping, approval mode, subdelegation flag, expiry and credential reference name. 3. Read back the map and effective policy. Confirm the peer is not mapped as `vp`. 4. Send a signed fixture request in an allowed scope. Require local actor provenance, `peer_request_id`, dedupe and an approval decision where configured. 5. Confirm the local objective/ticket is created only after the policy decision. 6. Confirm peer reports correlate to local ticket/report ids. 7. Test an out-of-scope request and a payload asserting `as: vp`; expect audited denial or policy-selected wait, with no local dispatch or grant.

## Evidence
Retain map key/revision, scope decision, approval/deny/wait record, peer request id, local actor, ticket/objective/report refs, and the audit record. Revoke or retire the map through the controller; do not delete the evidence.
